pass_a_gloss: Let us keep in mind that, happening to be in this life and understanding the roads outside life, we say to God the saying: you bent aside our tracks from your road. Now is a season to be reminded of the fact that this land, in which we have been humbled, is a place of ill treatment of the soul; so that praying we may say the saying: because you humbled us in a place of ill treatment, and a shade of death covered over us. And being bold we say also the saying: if we forgot the name of our God, and if we stretched wide our hands toward an alien god, will God not seek out these things?
pass_b_english: Let us remember that, while we are in this life and perceive the ways that lie outside this life, we say to God: “You have turned our paths aside from your way” (Psalm 44:18). Now is the time to recall that this region, in which we have been brought low, is a place of affliction for the soul, so that in prayer we may say: “For you brought us low in a place of affliction, and the shadow of death covered us” (Psalm 44:19). And with confidence we also say: “If we have forgotten the name of our God, and if we have spread out our hands to a foreign god, will not God search this out?” (Psalm 44:20-21).

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. 20); the old English was a digest. The old English replaced this chapter with lines from chapter 21 (sheep for slaughter, Proverbs 7:1) and an invented sentence about sheep among wolves; Origen's reading of Psalm 44:18-21 was lost.
Monuovevousev read Μνημονεύσωμεν; Havarov read θανάτου; λέyousv καὶ 10‘ read λέγομεν καὶ τό; „ori read ὅτι.
Koetschau prints M: φαμεν τό (P and Delarue φαμεν ὅτι) and 'now is the time to recall' (P and Delarue 'we must recall'). English follows Koetschau.
'A place of affliction' (of ill treatment) for the soul; τεταπεινώμεθα 'we have been brought low'.
